newsitem.title: USA: ITT stock leaps on speculation of higher bid.
newsitem.headline: ITT stock leaps on speculation of higher bid.

text.p: The stock of ITT Corp. jumped more than $15 on Tuesday as Wall Street anticipated Hilton Hotels Corp. would have to raise its $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ITT.
ITT rose as high as $58.875 a share in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange, exceeding the $55 a share that Hilton bid late Monday.

Stock traders who specialise in takeovers said they didn't expect any other companies to engage Hilton in a bidding war, but they expected ITT to put up enough of a fight to force Hilton to raise its bid.

"I think the price could go higher," said one trader who spoke on condition he not be identified. "It looks like a typical hostile (offer) and Hilton will be forced to pay more. They will end up bidding against themselves because I can see no white knight out there," the trader said.
Hilton Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach stuck tight to his $55 bid Tuesday, saying a higher bid would come only after meeting with ITT management.
"I don't think we need to change the price unless we meet with ITT," Bollenbach said in a telephone conference call.

Bollenbach said he would consider a higher price only if, after meeting with ITT executives, Hilton determined ITT had greater value. Any price hike would need to meet Hilton's goal of ensuring the deal would add to earnings, he said.
Wall Street analysts speculated that ITT, a hotel, gambling and entertainent company, would have to devise a clever defence to fend off its rival.
ITT may have leeway to use the courts to block a takeover because it is incorporated in Nevada, a state with tough anti-takeover laws, they said.
ITT was part of a huge conglomerate until 1995, when it spun off its manufacturing operations as ITT Industries and its insurance division as ITT Hartford Group Inc.
ITT Chief Executive Rand Araskog has run the company since 1979 and took over as top executive after the spin-off.
In early afternoon ITT stock was up $14.875 at $57.50. Hilton also gained, trading at $28.375, up $3.125 on the NYSE.
Bollenbach said Monday a merged Hilton and ITT corporation could cut costs by an estimated $100 million by consolidating their reservations systems and reducing management overhead.
"It's economics that compel these things, and we have the opportunity to put together a company that is simply more economical," Bollenbach said in an interview.

In addition, Hilton could scale scale back ITT's $3 billion capital spending programme for new hotels and casinos in Las Vegas and Atlantic City because if built, the new operations would overlap current plans.

Hilton also will look at shedding ITT's non-core entertainment assets such as MSG Limited Partnership, owner of Madison Square Garden sports arena, an all-sports cable network and the New York Knicks professional basketball team and New York Rangers hockey team.

But David Wolfe, financial analyst at Oppenheimer & Co., said the entertainment assets would not fetch anything near the roughly $1 billion ITT paid for them. ITT said late Monday it would take 10 days to review the offer.
